questions.question: Describe the Revolt of the Northern Earls in 1569. (4 marks)

points.text: In November 1569, the Earls of Northumberland (Thomas Percy) and Westmorland (Charles Neville) gathered approximately 4,500 armed men and marched into Durham, where they celebrated a Catholic Mass in the Cathedral. questions.question: Explain how Walsingham's spy network uncovered the Babington Plot. (4 marks)

points.text: Walsingham uncovered the Babington Plot by: infiltrating the conspiracy with a double agent (Gilbert Gifford); intercepting Mary's letters, which were smuggled in beer barrels; having his secretary Thomas Phelippes decode the letters using cipher; waiting until Mary wrote back approving the assassination of Elizabeth on 17 July 1586. questions.question: Why did Elizabeth hesitate before signing Mary Queen of Scots' death warrant? (4 marks)

points.text: Elizabeth hesitated because: executing a fellow monarch was unprecedented and set a dangerous precedent; Mary was her cousin; she feared provoking an invasion by Catholic powers (especially Spain); she worried about the reaction of Mary's son, James VI of Scotland; she was uncertain about the morality of the execution. questions.question: Compare the Ridolfi Plot and the Babington Plot. In what ways were they similar and different? (8 marks)

points.text: Similarities: both plots aimed to replace Elizabeth with Mary Queen of Scots; both had foreign Catholic backing; both were discovered by Walsingham's network; both led to executions of the key plotters.
